newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian senate delays vote on German art treasures.
newsitem.headline: Russian senate delays vote on German art treasures.

text.p: Russia's upper house of parliament on Wednesday delayed a vote on the fate of art treasures the Soviet Red Army seized from Nazi Germany during World War Two.
Deputies decided to hold a written ballot on a law which would keep the art works in Russia, which means a final result could be delayed until May.
The lower house has already passed the law, overruling a veto from President Boris Yeltsin, who left on Wednesday for a two-day trip to Germany.
The Federation Council had been discussing a law asserting Russian ownership of the art, which include treasures from ancient Troy, a priceless Gutenberg bible and French impressionist works.
Mikhail Mashkovtsev, local parliament head in the remote Kamchatka region, said all deputies should vote on the issue, something which involves a lengthy procedure of written ballots.
"All deputies...including those absent from the hall, should be responsible for this law," he said.
Deputies said Yeltsin had urged leaders of the upper house not to overrule his veto during his visit to Germany, where officials are seeking the return of the art.
The art has become a pressing issue half a century after World War Two because Russia has admitted holding a far bigger collection of trophy art than it previously acknowleged.

In an interview published on Tuesday, Yeltsin, asked by the German magazine Stern if he would bring some of the art treasures in his luggage to Germany, said: "Not the Troy gold, of course. But I'll bring some other items with me."

Many Russians view the art, seized from museums and homes in Nazi Germany, its allies and occupied countries, as compensation for the wartime suffering of the Soviet people and for the many Russian treasures destroyed in the brutal German invasion.
Yeltsin's promise to bring some art with him to Germany angered Russian ultranationalist leader Vladimir Zhirinovsky.
"They annihilated 26 millions Russian citizens and we have to pay them, it appears. They are scoundrels, fascists and bastards," he told a news conference.
